references.title: GRADE Handbook
references.summary: Certainty of evidence rated high, moderate, low or very low. Randomized trials start high and observational studies low; certainty drops for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias, and rises for a large effect or a dose-response gradient.

stance.why: The four levels and the start-then-downgrade method are kept; study design becomes the kind of signal (behavior starts high, stated intent low), indirectness becomes audience fit and imprecision becomes sample size.

references.title: The Mom Test
references.summary: Ask about people's lives and past behavior, not about your idea; compliments, generalities and hypotheticals are not data, and commitment is the real signal.

stance.why: Its ranking of signals (commitment over compliments, past facts over hypotheticals) sets the starting grades and the specificity downgrade; its method is the problem-interview template.

references.title: The top 9 reasons startups fail
references.summary: Analysis of startup post-mortems; poor product-market fit was cited in 43% of failures (causes overlap).

stance.why: The most common cause of failure is building what the market does not need, so a validation claim with no evidence grades very low instead of passing.
